summary: modelsdesk ships obfuscated Function-constructor payload in CLI bin shim
details: bin/modelsd.js presents itself as a short platform-binary resolver but contains a ~13KB obfuscated IIFE hidden after a long run of tab padding. The file defines a custom seeded Fisher-Yates shuffle decoder (spin/peel/splitLane), encodes all numeric constants via XOR-literal pairs (e.g. 648486^648486), and references standard String/Array methods such as charAt, length, substring, join, split, and fromCharCode via \uXXXX escapes to evade static analysis. The decoder produces two strings that are passed to peel.constructor (the Function constructor) and invoked with (global, require), giving the decoded code full module-level host access, including require() of arbitrary built-ins, on every invocation of the modelsd CLI. Structural anomalies corroborate injection into an otherwise trivial shim: duplicate `import { createRequire }` statements and duplicate `const require = createRequire(import.meta.url)` declarations coexist with the visible shim logic, and SKILL.md documents modeldesk as a Rust CLI installed via `cargo install`, inconsistent with an npm JS distribution whose primary payload is an opaque Function-constructor eval. The combination of cover-story shim, anti-analysis obfuscation, and dynamic code construction with (global, require) is a hostile code-execution pattern targeting any host that runs the modelsd CLI.
